focus: case lifecycle lock hold interval across authorization and protected opens
summary: PSK-SEC17-01 is closed in the current SDD. The case OS lifecycle lock is explicitly held from before the second catalog authorization until the operation finishes and all DB/sidecar/key handles are closed. Cleanup retains the same lock from durable quarantine through deletion, parent Sync, and tombstone. The acceptance matrix now specifies both cleanup-wins stale-snapshot rejection and opener-wins contention where cleanup waits until handles close, plus bounded completion. Case-before-catalog ordering and the prohibition on catalog-to-case acquisition remain consistent, with no lock cycle apparent. No new design blocker was found.

round17_dispositions.evidence: §3 specifies continuous lifecycle-lock ownership from before the second catalog re-read through operation completion and closure of all SQLite/DB/sidecar/key handles. Cleanup holds that lock through quarantine append+Sync, deletion, parent-directory Sync, and tombstone append+Sync. §6 adds the opener-wins contention case and preserves cleanup-wins stale-snapshot rejection.

control_dispositions.two_phase_catalog_authorization: coherent: optimistic read is revalidated under catalog lock only after case lock acquisition; protected opens occur while case lock remains held
control_dispositions.cleanup_wins: opener rechecks current catalog after acquiring case lock and rejects before DB open after quarantine/tombstone
control_dispositions.opener_wins: cleanup waits while authorized opener retains case lock and active handles; cleanup proceeds after close/release, later opener rejects before DB open
control_dispositions.lock_order: case lifecycle lock then catalog lock; catalog holders never wait for case lock; no cycle apparent
control_dispositions.cleanup_failure: quarantine is durable before deletion; lock remains held through failure handling, then fail-closed state is preserved before release

limitations: No tests or runtime validation were run.
No OS lock primitive, filesystem handle, SQLite connection, process contention, or cleanup path was exercised.
Approval is limited to the written design under its declared test-only trusted-local-account boundary; it does not establish implementation correctness or classroom readiness.
